references.name: text-embeddings-inference
references.procedure: POST /decode then /tokenize to check the rows survive TEI's re-tokenization; then POST /embed with the batch's 32 rows as token ids, 5 untimed then 50 timed, each timed from sending the request to reading the whole response, the p50 and p99 of TEI's x-total-time, x-tokenization-time, x-queue-time, x-inference-time headers beside it, and TEI's /metrics read before and after the timed requests for its te_batch_next_size and te_batch_next_tokens histograms; min_cosine is against the bundle's reference vectors; TEI's router built natively and run on this machine, not in a container; round trip (measured) p50 1109.852 ms, p99 1202.664 ms; TEI's own headers, whole ms, over the same requests: x-total-time p50 1108 p99 1199, x-tokenization-time p50 2 p99 16, x-queue-time p50 208 p99 327, x-inference-time p50 697 p99 1153; TEI's /metrics over the timed requests: 1600 inputs in 50 requests, 146 backend batches (te_batch_next_size's 260 samples less the 114 empty polls te_batch_next_tokens shows), 2.92 batches per request, mean batch size 10.96 inputs (batches by size, 1: 23, 2: 16, 3 to 4: 18, 5 to 8: 24, 9 to 16: 18, 17 to 32: 47); the tool ran unpinned; TEI ran unpinned with the image's thread settings: OMP_NUM_THREADS=unset, MKL_NUM_THREADS=unset, RAYON_NUM_THREADS=unset

references.name: mlx
references.procedure: MLX 0.29.3 on the machine's Python, the BERT encoder of bench/reference/mlx_reference.py with every weight cast to float16, mx.compile, mean pooling and L2 in F32, on the same token rows as a padded batch; untimed runs, then 50 timed as host wall time, each waited for with mx.eval, the rows already on the device and the vectors not read back: min 102.9470 ms, mean 104.8950 ms. min_cosine is against each row's expected vector. Host load averages before the runs 2.95 3.35 4.87.
